content:
maya: quick heads-up — ran the int4 ensemble canary (raven-lite + kestrel fallback) on the prod mirror and saw funcall parse failures jump from ~0.9% to 3.8%
oliver: ouch. same promptset as last run?
maya: same batch, but i didn’t enable deterministic_seed for the ensemble ordering. replayed a few failing requests — failures correlate with fallback ordering (kestrel firing after raven-lite).
sasha: any signs it s tokenization vs serialization suffix noise?
maya: logs show partial JSON fragments: first model emits something like "{\"action\": \"call\", \"args\": {\"q\": 1"
then fallback appends ", \"extra\": true}}" which becomes invalid for our strict parser.
raj: sounds like inter-model suffix overlap. our ensemble aggregator concatenates raw token streams — no separator. should we force NDJSON boundaries per-model?
maya: that s my thought. when fallback happens mid-object, the second model continues assuming fresh output.
oliver: plan: 1) run deterministic replay for 1k requests with fixed ordering to rule out RNG, 2) capture per-model token boundary sentinels in traces.
infra-bot: canary summary: dedicated_canary_2026-03-21, 60k requests, baseline_parse_err 0.38% -> canary_parse_err 3.82%
sasha: short-term mitigation: wrap each model s output in a single-line NDJSON envelope so aggregator can merge safely, e.g. "{\"__model\":\"raven-lite\",\"body\":{...}}" then merge bodies preferring earliest model.
maya: avoids token collisions but changes downstream contract and adds postprocess cost.
raj: alternative: inject a synthetic separator token between model streams (a nonprintable sentinel models won t generate) and strip it before parse. hacky but minimal interface change.
oliver: also add a fuzz test in the eval harness that simulates mid-token fallback: cut generation at random token and append fallback output. cheap way to catch regressions pre-canary.
sasha: prototyping NDJSON merge now. quick pseudo in aggregator postprocess:
```python
# aggregator merge prototype
parts = [json.loads(line) for line in stream.splitlines()]
merged = {}
for p in parts:
    merged.update(p.get('body', {}))
return json.dumps(merged)
```
raj: keep __model keys if we want provenance, or track model->field mapping.
maya: action items:
- oliver: enable deterministic_seed and replay 1k requests (EOD)
- sasha: push NDJSON wrapper PR to branch canary-ndjson-merge (tomorrow)
- raj: add trace flags for per-model token boundaries (toggleable perf hit)
- infra: create metric "ensemble-token-boundary-collisions" and alerting rule
infra-bot: ticket INF-2026-378 created and assigned to oliver/sasha/raj, severity P2
maya: thanks — oliver, post the replay summary and attach raw failing examples when ready :thumbsup:
